text: ATM Audience Dashboard · updated Nov 2, 2026 · daily figures refresh on open · monthly figures Oct 1–31
Site sessions more than doubled on Awards voting, LinkedIn grew on more posts, and accepted collabs drove Instagram views.

Moment Awards voting brought 6,119 people to the /vote page, and site sessions more than doubled on September (+111%). 96% of voting sessions went to no other page, and without voting, sessions were between 9.6% down and 1.0% up on September. LinkedIn impressions rose 8.4% and reactions 18.5% on more posts; comments held level. Single-guest interview cuts drew a median 737 impressions, against 262 for the Top 20 and voting posts. On Instagram, posts with an accepted collaborator drew a median 959 views, against 293 without, and 18 of 45 posts had one. Reposts with the reposter's own words lifted engagement 1.34×, above September's 1.28×. YouTube views fell 22%, with 57% coming from YouTube search. The newsletter grew 64% on imports (figures to Oct 27).

Sources: Supermetrics (LinkedIn Pages, Instagram Insights, YouTube, GA4), pulled Nov 2 for the full month; Instagram collaborator status read on each post's page Nov 2; LinkedIn Reposts lists read Nov 2; the October report (Oct 28) for the newsletter (beehiiv, to Oct 27); monday.com and the TEAM ATM live links. Daily figures refresh each time the page opens.
The read · October 1 to 31, 2026
What the numbers say, and what to do about it

One reading of the October report and the daily figures, checked against what the team changed and when. Each point cites the section that holds the evidence. Reads of why a post did well are hypotheses.

title: Awards voting more than doubled site sessions; the rest of the site was flat to down.
text: atm.media drew 13,141 sessions and 11,079 users in October, more than double September's 6,218 sessions (+111%). Moment Awards voting accounts for more than the whole rise: 7,529 sessions included a /vote page, and 96% of them (about 7,200) went to no other page. Without voting, sessions changed between −9.6% and +1.0% on September: −9.6% when every session that touched /vote is removed, +1.0% when only sessions that started on /vote are removed. About 300 sessions included both voting and another page, and 182 of those started on /vote and went on to other content. Episode pages grew 4.8% to 3,538 views. (At a glance; B)

title: LinkedIn reached more on more posts; comments per post fell.
text: Organic impressions were 58,394 in October, up 8.4% on September, and reactions rose 18.5% to 1,830. Comments held level at 173 against 174, on about half again as many posts, so comments per post fell. Single-guest interview cuts (18 posts) drew a median 737 impressions; the 26 Top 20 and voting posts drew a median 262. Followers reached 4,201 on Oct 31. (At a glance; B; E)

title: Reposts with the reposter's own words lifted engagement by a third.
text: Reposts that carried the reposter's own words added 718 engagements to 2,130 organic across all 65 October posts: 1.34×, against 1.28× in September. 47 of the 172 reposts had commentary; the other 125 were plain reposts. Guests drove most of it: Keri Denise Richardson's own repost of her AAF Hall of Achievement cut drew 123 engagements and Amanda Forrester's 98. The Oct 28 report read 1.02× from 16 posts; the full read covers every post and the engagement reposts gathered since. (C; E)

title: On Instagram, posts with an accepted collaborator drew about three times the views.
text: The 18 posts with an accepted collaborator drew a median 959 views; the 27 without drew a median 293, about a third as many. Collaborator status was read on each post's page on Nov 2, so it includes three invites accepted after Oct 27. Account views were 58,843 in October, down 8.8% on September, and reach was 28,301. The Top 20 carousel was the month's best post (6,148 views), shared on by nominees. (At a glance; B; E)

title: The newsletter grew on imports; clicks held.
text: Active subscribers reached 13,794 by Oct 27, up 64%, and 5,588 of the 5,753 adds were imports (3,045 of them on Oct 26–27, after the last send). The open rate fell to 34.4% from 43.4% as the list grew, while verified human clicks rose 48% to 354 and held at 0.53% of delivered email. These figures stop at Oct 27, so the Oct 30 issue is not counted. (At a glance; B; 02)

title: YouTube views fell; most come from YouTube search.
text: 3,461 views in October, down 22% on September's 4,421, all organic, with +26 net subscribers. YouTube search brought 57% of views and the Shorts feed 18%; links from outside YouTube brought under 5%, so the site and newsletter send few viewers. (At a glance; B)

title: Ask for the collab and a first-hour comment in every live-links email.
text: Posts with an accepted Instagram collaborator drew about three times the views, and 27 of 45 October posts had none. Put "please accept the Instagram collab" and a like or comment in the first hour into the live-links email, and follow up after a day. Target: half of Instagram posts with an accepted collaborator.

title: Hand guests and partners repost copy on publish day.
text: The biggest lifts came from guests reposting with their own words (Keri Denise Richardson, Amanda Forrester), while 125 of 172 reposts carried no comment. Send guests and partners a ready line they can post with the link, and check the Reposts list two days later.

title: Turn voters into readers.
text: After Nov 5, send the voters a welcome email and track their 30-day verified clicks apart from the imports, so the Awards traffic can be judged on what it leaves behind.

title: Post fewer sizzles and more people.
text: Single-guest interview cuts drew a median 737 LinkedIn impressions in October, almost three times the 262 for Top 20 and voting posts. Cap Top 5 and winner posts at one a day, and keep two interview cuts a week on LinkedIn.

title: Rest repeat guests and widen the bench.
text: Michelle Crossan-Matos has five appearances all-time, three of them in October. Meredith Diehn's third piece in about three weeks drew 108 LinkedIn impressions, and Barbara Peng also dipped on the repeat. Rest all three on social after Nov 5, space repeat guests further apart, and book Publicis and IPG voices, and CPG and pharma marketers beyond PepsiCo, Hello Products and Organon.

title: Give every guest and partner the exact tag.
text: Put "@At The Moment Media (ATM)" and the page link in the ready caption you send them, so nobody picks the similar page from LinkedIn's autocomplete.

title: Check the tag before anything goes live.
text: Add one line to the go-live checklist: any tag of ATM points to the ATM page, not "At The Moment". Check partner drafts the same way when they share them.

title: Watch the other page's follower jumps.
text: The daily run already reads the competitor table. Flag any week "At The Moment" gains followers without posting, and line it up with ATM's posts that week: a jump right after a big ATM post points to mis-tags or mis-follows.

title: Log what you find.
text: Add a "tagged to the wrong page" column to the tagging audit, so the count shows month to month and you can tell whether the fixes work.

title: Rob and Hannah: move the Supermetrics data connections to a shared ATM login.
text: GA4, Search Console and YouTube connect through Rob's personal Google login, and LinkedIn through Hannah's. Instagram already uses the ATM account. If a personal login is disconnected, the daily social pull, the weekly GA4 pull and the monthly run stop.

title: Hannah: share the live optimization log.
text: So each monthly run can read it directly. The testing tracker in monday.com feeds the Briefings tab once it exists.

title: Rob and Dan: make utm_content the content ID on every link.
text: Use the episode slug as utm_content whatever the source, so several UTM links to one piece of content add up to that piece. Keep a small lookup sheet for older links.

title: Matt: add episode-level site and YouTube pulls for partner profiles.
text: Add per-page GA4 sessions and per-video YouTube views to the scheduled pulls, matched to partners by episode URL and video title. Partner profiles in Briefings can then show site visits to each partner's episode pages and views of the full episodes.

title: utm_partner does not show in GA4 reports.
text: GA4 reads only its standard UTM fields, so utm_partner is dropped. Put the partner in utm_term (standard, unused today) on every link from now on, next to the episode slug in utm_content.

title: Newsletter traffic lands in "Unassigned".
text: beehiiv tags it newsletter and the episode links use owned_audience; GA4 files both as Unassigned. Set the medium to email, or add a channel group that joins them.

title: Every GA4 event is marked as a key event.
text: Engaged sessions, bounce rate and conversions mean nothing until the default events are unmarked. The fix only works going forward.

title: The Looker subscriber card is stale.
text: It has read 5,642 since Aug 31 while beehiiv reports far more. Re-point it, or retire it in favour of beehiiv.

title: Searches in the library are not tracked.
text: The site has no search bar of its own, and the library search fills results as people type without changing the address, so GA4's site search setting cannot see it. Ask whoever maintains the library to send a GA4 "search" event with the typed words as search_term once a visitor stops typing for about a second. The terms then show under Search term in GA4.

title: Episode links on social cuts have no UTM of their own.
text: Without one, traffic from the link layer cannot be told apart in GA4.

title: Internal visits count as site traffic.
text: In the 30 days to Oct 18, 366 sessions came from Microsoft Teams, Office documents and the site editor, mostly the team and partners opening links. Add an internal-traffic filter in GA4 so they drop out.

title: One piece of content appears under several utm_content spellings.
text: GA4 shows the same episode as "Nick Primola - Group EVP...", "NickPrimola-GroupEVP..." and "Nick", and the Deloitte episode three ways. Taking utm_content from the episode URL ending fixes this going forward.

title: Episode pages cannot rank in Google.
text: About 190 of 220 episode pages show no search impressions. Add a title tag, meta description, video schema, publish date and transcript to the episode template, clean up the slugs, and submit a video sitemap in Search Console.

title: Imported newsletter subscribers get no welcome email.
text: The welcome flow has enrolled 12 people since July while thousands were imported. Turn on a welcome automation for imports in beehiiv, and decide on double opt-in for cold sources. Referral milestones are also not set up.

title: Instagram follower demographics are not read.
text: They need a Meta Business Suite login, which no current run uses.

title: No play counts per episode.
text: Vimeo is not connected, so sponsor recaps cannot show plays per episode or per partner series.

title: overview
text: Moment Awards voting ran from the Oct 6 Top 20 reveal to Oct 30 (extended), and the Awards are on Nov 5. Most of October's site traffic is voting.

title: overview
text: ATM posted about half again as many LinkedIn originals as in September, many of them Top 20 sizzles, so totals rose while reach per post fell.

title: B
text: October 2026 is the full month, Oct 1–31, from Supermetrics pulled Nov 2. LinkedIn months before July include no sponsored impressions on this chart.

title: C
text: Repost tracking began in September (17 posts checked). October reads every post's Reposts list, on Nov 2.
3,045 imported subscribers arrived on Oct 26–27, after the last October send, so their first opens and clicks fall in November.

title: Followers.
text: LinkedIn's own total was 4,201 on Oct 31. The daily follower chart tracks organic gains from a fixed starting point, so it reads lower; use it for the trend, not the total.

title: Engagement rate.
text: LinkedIn's own rate counts clicks. The Overview scorecards leave clicks out so months compare on the same terms.

title: Time windows.
text: Monthly figures cover the full month, Oct 1–31, against Sep 1–30. The newsletter is still partial (to Oct 27; beehiiv is not connected). Daily figures run to the latest day each platform has reported.

title: Sources this month.
text: The Oct 28 report read the platforms' own dashboards because the Supermetrics connection failed on that run. The full-month figures here are from Supermetrics on Nov 2; YouTube in particular reports two to three days late, so the Nov 1 pull undercounted it (3,195 against 3,461).

title: Subscribers.
text: beehiiv's active count includes imported addresses, so list size alone overstates readers; verified clicks are the better measure.

title: LinkedIn collab posts.
text: Records disagree on whether the feature is live on the ATM page, and the Oct 6 check found no collab option. Until that is settled, no figure on this page assumes it.

title: "At The Moment".
text: A separate LinkedIn page with a similar name, not an ATM page. It stays in the peer set and is watched for follows and tags meant for ATM.
